instructions.note: The prompt authorizes the agent to use its own judgment on partial refunds and explicitly forbids confirmation, leaving refund amount selection broad and unchecked.

findings.title: Missing attributable refund provenance for irreversible refunds executed under a shared service account

forecast.watch_signal: Refund volume, unattended runtime, or refund authority scope increases without adding requester-bound provenance and retention controls.

evidence.observation: The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool.
The processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why.
The agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Bind each refund to the authenticated staff identity and business justification in an immutable audit record retained longer than the refund settlement and dispute window.
Replace the shared service account with requester-bound or delegated credentials so refund actions are attributable to the initiating staff member.
Require a second-party approval or case-linked authorization for partial refunds above a defined threshold.

findings.title: Confused deputy refund authority via shared service account on irreversible spend capability

attack_path.note: Authenticated staff request can directly influence refund execution.
Agent can issue irreversible refunds through the payments processor.

forecast.watch_signal: Refund scope widens beyond current business limits or the agent is allowed to run more autonomously without requester-bound identity controls.

evidence.observation: The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool.
payments.issue_refund can refund any order and any amount up to the order total.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.
The prompt directs the agent to check the order and then issue the refund, and says not to ask for confirmation.

recommendations.action: Use delegated staff identity or per-tool least-privilege credentials that enforce who may refund which orders and amounts.
Constrain refund capability by policy thresholds, allowable order ownership, and case linkage at the payment API boundary.

findings.title: Trusted staff request can trigger irreversible refund with no approval and instruction-level discretion on amount

attack_path.note: Trusted support staff request enters the agent context.
Agent reads order history and payment details to decide refund handling.

forecast.watch_signal: Prompt or product changes that broaden refund purpose or allow the agent to process larger unattended queues without adding structural checks.

evidence.observation: The prompt says to process refund requests from support staff, check the order, then issue the refund.
The prompt says to use judgment on partial refunds and not ask for confirmation.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate or explicit policy engine for partial refunds and higher-value refunds before the refund API call executes.
Tighten the prompt to require objective refund policy checks and to refuse ambiguous or unsupported refund amounts.

The request channel is said to be SSO authenticated, but the artifacts do not describe session binding or anti-impersonation controls.

The artifacts do not describe who can read processor logs or whether refund records expose sensitive payment details.
No design fact suggests availability of the processor log store is security-critical to refund execution itself in this case.

Loss of chat history after retention is a provenance problem here, not a service availability control for refund execution.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by missing attributable provenance for irreversible refunds executed through a shared service account. Additional present risks remain moderate for confused deputy authority and unchecked irreversible refund execution from trusted staff requests. No declared or verified controls reduce the residual tier. Forecast remains high because the current design already lacks the key structural controls; increases in scope, autonomy, or task horizon would preserve or worsen the same exposure. Manual validation only; scripts were not runnable in this environment.

limitations: Assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, tool manifest, API policy, or processor-side authorization configuration was provided, so credential scope and enforcement are rated from the notes only.
No runtime telemetry or audit implementation evidence was available, so findings about provenance and limits are based on declared logging and retention behavior.
Because the artifacts do not describe volume limits, approval workflows, or refund policy thresholds, denial-of-service and approval-strength questions remain lower-confidence or not assessed.
